author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list treats a page number below 1 as the first page
summary: Requesting the owner list with page 0 or a negative page shows the first page of the normal listing with a success response instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a request for the owner list at page 0, when it runs, then the response is HTTP 200 and the normal owner listing for the first page is rendered
given a request for the owner list at a negative page, when it runs, then the response is HTTP 200 and the normal owner listing for the first page is rendered
given a page value below 1, when the listing is rendered, then the owners shown are the same as for page 1
non_goals: page values that are not numbers
page values beyond the last page
page-size changes or other changes to owner search behavior
notes: Scope quoted from intake line 1: 'the owner listing treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal listing (HTTP 200)'. One data-driven test covers the rows page=0 and page=-1. No Non-Goals row is touched. The non_goals listed above are slice exclusions the intake does not mention. They are left open and do not record any decision. Root observation, not a requirement: the cause sits where the page number becomes a zero-based page index.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by system-design.md § Contracts (OwnerController row: search with paging) and architecture-principles.md § pattern catalog, Web controller row, which says that normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule. The cause, found by grep (no IDE oracle connected, so this is the weaker basis): OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize). For page < 1 that index is negative, so PageRequest throws IllegalArgumentException and the error page renders. The fix belongs in OwnerController.processFindForm, the binding site: clamp the bound page to at least 1 once, before both the repository query and addPaginationModel, so currentPage in the model matches the page actually served. No new type, module, or pattern. The only design-doc write is REQ-OWN-005 joining the OwnerController Contracts row.
integration_points: Binding target: the existing GET /owners handler binds page as an int request parameter (a request-scoped primitive) and Owner as a search probe under the existing setAllowedFields disallow list. The slice adds no entry point and no new bound field.

Double for the repository boundary: the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository in OwnerControllerTests, matching the suite's established and tolerated stub. The test should assert that the Pageable passed to findByLastNameStartingWith has page index 0 for page=0 and page=-1, for example by argument capture or an argThat on getPageNumber, so that 'same owners as page 1' is proven at the query.
Double for the framework transport: MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock in the CLAUDE.md testing strategy. Assert status 200, view owners/ownersList, and model currentPage = 1.

patterns.description: Normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding and sits in the controller.
Existing paged-listing test shape (PageImpl stub + get('/owners?page=1')) to extend as a data-driven test over page=0 and page=-1

risks.risk: The model's currentPage keeps the raw value (0 or -1) while the query serves page 1, so the pager renders inconsistently
risks.mitigation: Normalize the page once at the top of processFindForm and use the normalized value for both the query and addPaginationModel (architecture-principles.md § Web controller row)

risks.risk: Owner list path scaling: system-design.md has no Scale and Load section. The slice adds no path that scales with data, because page size is fixed and the request is still one bounded page query
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: clamp with Math.max. No structural change.

notes: Autofix audit: the log has no design-doc-autofix records, so it was skipped. No ADR is written: the slice takes no decision with a trade-off. Non-numeric page values and pages beyond the last page stay out of scope per the prd-entry non_goals, so the implementer must not widen the handling to them.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Boundary validation strengthened, not weakened: OwnerController.java:97 `int page = Math.max(requestedPage, 1);` clamps the request-supplied page before `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` (OwnerController.java:134), so page 0, negatives, and Integer.MIN_VALUE no longer raise IllegalArgumentException into the error page that renders exception messages; Math.max cannot overflow.

Request-derived page reaches Thymeleaf preprocessing in ownersList.html:44 `th:href="@{'/owners?page=__${currentPage - 1}__'}"` (and :49), but the value is bound as a Java int by @RequestParam and clamped, so no request-supplied text enters expression evaluation; non-numeric input still fails type conversion at binding (unchanged behavior). This preprocessing use is pre-existing and not widened by the change.

No change to data-access shape: the page feeds a Spring Data Pageable into the derived query findByLastNameStartingWith; no string-concatenated query text. Spring Data computes the offset as a long, so a very large page yields an empty result rather than overflow (pre-existing upper-bound behavior, unchanged).

Binding surface unchanged: the explicit `name = "page"` keeps the external parameter name identical; @InitBinder at OwnerController.java:61 `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id");` still covers the Owner search binding.
No secrets, credentials, logging, file I/O, or new endpoints introduced in the diff (python3 scripts/changeset.py read in full: 5 production lines, 17 test lines, two doc-table edits).

Supply chain: no dependency change in this diff; no OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured (`grep -n -F -e dependencyCheck build.gradle` returned no match), so no NVD match ran in this review; resolved versions from ./gradlew dependencies are Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind 3.1.5.
